texts.preamble: In The Matter Of Suo Moto Public Interest ... vs State Of Chhattisgarh on 21 November, 2024 1 / 24 High Court Of Chhattisgarh At Bilaspur Wppil No. 92 of 2024
texts.facts: In Compliance of the Court's order dated 11.11.2024, an affidavit has been filed by Additional Chief Secretary, Forest and Climate Change, relevant paras of which are being reproduced below:- "5. DETAILS REGARDING THE TIGER DEATH INCIDENT IN BAINKUTHPUR FOREST DIVISION AS APPEARED IN THE NEWS ARTICLE OF THE TIMES OF INDIA ARTICLE DATED 10.11.2024 5.1. That, upon receiving information on 08.11.2024 regarding the discovery of the tiger carcass near Khankhopar Nala, Sonhat Range in Koriya Forest Division, immediately a Preliminary Offence Report (POR) was registered. A copy of POR dated 08.11.2024 is being attached and marked as ANNEXURE A/1. 5.2. That, apart from the above, other immediate steps were initiated, including: (i) Deployment of a rapid response team to secure the site. (ii) Conducting a detailed post-mortem examination by qualified veterinarians to ascertain the cause of death (iii) Collecting forensic evidence to determine the exact cause of death. In The Matter Of Suo Moto Public Interest ... vs State Of Chhattisgarh on 21 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/157673677/ 1 5.3. That a preliminary examination of the post- mortem report has revealed that the tiger's death might have been caused by poisoning, which led to labored breathing and ultimately resulted in asphyxia. Further, upon careful examination of Point No. 2(c) of the post mortem report, it was also observed that while all ribs were present, there was a fracture in the 10th rib on the left side. A copy of the post-mortem report of the tiger is annexed herewith and marked as ANNEXURE A/2. 5.4. That, it is further submitted that the tiger's body was intact and the viscera and other body parts were sent for detailed histopathological and toxicological examination to the Indian Veterinary Research Institute (IVRI), Izatnagar, Bareilly, Uttar Pradesh, vide a letter issued by the Office of the Divisional Forest Officer (DFO), Koriya, dated 09.11.2024. A copy of the letter dated 09.11.2024 is annexed herewith and marked as ANNEXURE A/3. 5.5. That, it is pertinent to mention that the Indian Veterinary Research Institute (IVRI), Izatnagar, Bareilly, provided a toxicological examination report vide letter dated 14.11.2024. In the report, samples of the lung, liver, kidney, heart, spleen, stomach, and intestinal contents were analyzed for the presence of heavy metals and commonly used insecticides. The samples tested negative for these toxicants. However, the results of the Histopathological Examination (HPE) are still awaited. A copy of the toxicological examination report dated 14.11.2024 is annexed herewith and marked as ANNEXURE A/4. 5.6. That, as per the established Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) for handling tiger deaths, the National Tiger Conservation Authority (NTCA) nominated Ms. Prajakta Hushangabadkar, Officer-in-Charge and Assistant Manager, Wildlife Trust of India (WII) to ensure appropriate SOP be followed to deal with tiger mortality that happened in Sonhat, Range, Koriya Division, Chhattisgarh vide letter dated 08.11.2024. A copy of the nomination letter dated 08.11.2024 is annexed herewith and marked as ANNEXURE A/5. 5.7. That, after all the relevant samples were collected from the body and the post-mortem analysis was completed, the body was disposed of through incineration as per the prescribed rules in the presence of the competent authority. A copy of the Panchanama of the incineration of the tiger's body dated 09.11.2024, is annexed herewith and marked as ANNEXURE A/6. 5.8. At this juncture, it is pertinent to mention that a senior forest officer i.e. Additional PCCF (Wildlife) visited the site of the tiger's death on 09.11.2024 and provided detailed instructions to the field officers regarding the further course of action. He also submitted a comprehensive report on the case to the state government vide letter dated 14.11.2024. A copy of the APCCF (Wildlife) report dated 14.11.2024 is annexed herewith and marked as ANNEXURE -A/7. 5.9. That, upon receiving the report dated 14.11.2024, the disciplinary action was initiated, therefore, one Forest Guard, Mr. Pitambar Lal Rajwade, one Range Assistant, Mr. Raman Pratap Singh, and one Range Officer (Forest), Mr. Vinay Kumar Singh, were suspended. Copies of suspension orders are annexed herewith and collectively marked as ANNEXUREA/8 (colly). In The Matter Of Suo Moto Public Interest ... vs State Of Chhattisgarh on 21 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/157673677/ 2 5.10. That, four investigation teams were constituted for field investigation by the Divisional Forest Officer (DFO), Koriya Forest Division. The said Investigation Teams have made field investigation and submitted its daily reports. Copies of the orders of team formation, along with their daily reports, are annexed herewith and collectively marked as ANNEXURE A/9 (colly). 5.11. That, even Chief Wildlife Warden of Chhattisgarh also completed his field visit in the nearby areas of Gurughasidas Tiger Reserve where Tiger movements were intercepted and he took meetings of the ground staff and villagers in various villages and tried to improvise the relations and ensured them timely compensation and their safety. 5.12. That, the deponent most humbly and respectfully submits that from the aforesaid it appears that all established procedures and protocols prescribed under the relevant rules and guidelines have been meticulously adhered to in the instant case. She further ensures that each step undertaken conforms to the prescribed legal and administrative frameworks, leaving scope for no procedural deviation. Furthermore, appropriate corrective measures have been promptly initiated and implemented by the answering respondent to address any lapses or deficiencies identified during the course of the investigation. At the cost of repetition, the deponent reiterates its commitment to ensure that the matter is dealt with in a manner that upholds the principles of fairness, accountability, and compliance with the rule of law to preserve the wildlife in the state of Chhattisgarh. 6. DETAILS REGARDING ELEPHANT CALF HURT BY "POTASH BOMB" IN UDANTI SITANADI TIGER RESERVE AS APPEARED IN THE NEWS ARTICLE OF TIMES OF INDIA DATED 12.11.2024 6.1. That, the deponent most humbly submits that a news article published in The Times of India dated 12.11.2024 reported an incident involving an elephant calfinjured by a "potash bomb" in the Udanti-Sitanadi Tiger Reserve 6.2. That, upon receiving information about the incident, the Forest Range Officer, Mr. Shailesh Baghel, conducted an immediate investigation at the site of the incident. All materials of forensic importance were collected from the location for detailed examination. Pursuant to the investigation, a Preliminary Offense Report (POR) was registered as Forest Crime No. 79/19 on 09.11.2024 under relevant provisions of the Wildlife Protection Act, 1972. A copy of the POR dated 09.11.2024 for injuring calf elephant is annexed herewith and marked as ANNEXURE A/10. 6.3. That, in connection with the aforementioned incident, the Deputy Director, Udanti Sitanadi Tiger Reserve, submitted a comprehensive report vide letter dated 12.11.2024, which provides the following details: a) Incident Details (07.11.2024): The incident of the Satlor Range, Sitanadi. Prima facie, it appears that the potash bomb was planted by an unidentified individual with the intent to harm or scare away the elephants. b) Search and Tracking Efforts (08.11.2024):A Dog Squad, along with a team of veterinarians, was deployed to investigate the incident and assist in locating the injured elephant. In The Matter Of Suo Moto Public Interest ... vs State Of Chhattisgarh on 21 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/157673677/ 3 c) Successful Location of Injured Elephant (10.11.2024): The injured elephant's location was successfully traced using a Thermal Drone Camera, enabling the authorities to proceed with appropriate measures for its rescue and treatment. 6.4. That, after continuous monitoring for more than a week, it was observed that the injuries sustained by the elephant calf were healing naturally. The calf remained in close association with its herd, and no signs of critical health deterioration were observed. 6.5. That, considering the health status of the injured elephant calf, the team of veterinarians deemed it appropriate not to capture the calf, which had already healed. This decision was made to avoid subjecting the calf to undue stress and trauma that could arise from darting and tranquilizing. Additionally, there was a risk that the calf might not be accepted back into its herd due to potential human imprints resulting from the capture and handling process. 6.6. That, the elephant calf is presently in good health and is moving with its herd, which is roaming the forest areas bordering the Udanti- Sitanadi Tiger Reserve. The calf is exhibiting normal behavior, and no further complications have been reported. A copy of the latest report from the Deputy Director, Udanti-Sitanadi Tiger Reserve is annexed herewith and marked as ANNEXURE A/11. 6.7. That, with regard to the individual responsible for planting the potash bomb, an investigation is currently underway. The concerned forest officials are actively working to identify and apprehend the perpetrator. The authorities are committed to ensuring that those responsible for this unlawful act are held accountable. 6.8. That, the deponent re-affirms its commitment to the protection and conservation of wildlife. DETAILS REGARDING THE DEATH OF A TUSKER (ELEPHANT) IN BALRAMPUR AS REPORTED IN THE TIMES OF INDIA ON 12.11.2024 7.1. That, the deponent respectfully submits that the news item published in the Times of India dated 12.11.2024 reported the unfortunate death of a male elephant (tusker) due to electrocution within the jurisdiction of the Balrampur Forest Division. 7.2. That, upon receiving information about the incident, the Divisional Forest Officer, Balrampur, initiated an investigation, and the following facts have been ascertained regarding the said incident: a) That, upon receipt of the information on 11.11.2024 concerning the death of an elephant aged approximately 11 years near Murka Village in the Balrampur Forest Division, a Preliminary Offence Report (POR) was immediately registered as Criminal Case No. 18926/23 dated 11.11.2024 under Sections 9, 50, 51(1), and 52 of the Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972. A copy of the POR dated 11.11.2024 for death of elephant is annexed herewith and marked as ANNEXURE A/12. In The Matter Of Suo Moto Public Interest ... vs State Of Chhattisgarh on 21 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/157673677/ 4 b) That, as per the Standard Operating Procedures (SOP) for handling cases involving the death of an elephant, the body was thoroughly examined by an expert veterinarian in the presence of Forest Officials. The Post-Mortem Examination Report and circumstantial evidence established that the cause of death was electrocution. A copy of the post mortem report, of the death of the elephant is annexed herewith and marked as ANNEXURE A/13. c) That, during the night of 10.11.2024, a herd of wild elephants was observed roaming in the vicinity of Murka Village, located within the Murka Forest Beat of the Balrampur Forest Division. Forest Officers were deployed to alert the villagers about the presence of the herd and to instruct them to refrain from disturbing the elephants. They were also explicitly directed to ensure the removal of any illegal electrical fencing that might have been installed. d) That, as per the investigation conducted by the Forest Department, it has been established that the death of the tusker was caused by electrocution from illegal electrical fencing installed by the accused, Mr. RambakasAyam, son of Mr. BabulalAyam. The said fencing was unlawfully set up around farmland adjacent to the forest 7.3. That, the illegal electrical fencing in question was reportedly connected to a high-voltage power source, which was laid out with the intent to deter wildlife, particularly elephants, from entering agricultural fields. 7.4. That, in light of the findings, the Forest Department has undertaken the following actions:- a) Immediate removal of the illegal electrical fencing in the area to prevent any further incidents.
